title: IBTR note's threshold almost used up: 4.7bp of room on 15 Oct
problem: The filled IBTR note (set on the 6 Oct curve) says the first $300,000 buys all ten payments unless yields fall more than about 0.2 points. On the note's own basis (WInS holdings' maturity dates, yields unchanged to 1 Jan 2027) the room was $6,552 / 22.7bp on 6 Oct, 13.9bp on 14 Oct and $1,376 / 4.7bp on 15 Oct; long yields are down about 0.15-0.20 points since 6 Oct (7y 5.15 to 5.00, 20y 5.68 to 5.48). MODEL: roughly 28% chance the cost is above $300k on 20 Oct, about 45% by 31 Dec. The note stays true as a dated, conditional statement. The risk is a reflection that states a current status ('0.16 points left', 'not triggered') which is false or on a different basis by the time it is read. Basis note: the 16 Oct number sheet's $294,453 / $5,547 prices $50k on each 1 Jan payment date with forward rates; L05's $298,624 / $1,376 prices $50k on each WInS holding's earlier maturity with yields unchanged (dates explain about $3,390, curve assumption about $780; verify/L05w/decomp.py).

title: Two ladder-cost bases now in circulation ($294,453 vs $298,624 on 15 Oct); name one
problem: The 16 Oct number sheet (unmerged branch, which the branch CLAUDE.md tells the team to use for the IPS) prices the ten payments at $294,453, room $5,547 (~19bp). The IBTR note, MONITOR.md and lenses L03/L05/L08 use $298,624, room $1,376 (4.7bp). Same payments, same valuation date (1 Jan 2027), same curve date and bootstrap. Difference: the sheet puts each $50k on the 1 Jan payment date and rolls the curve on forwards (assumes cash waiting between maturity and payment earns forward rates); L05 puts it on each WInS holding's earlier maturity (15 Dec 2032 ... 15 Nov 2041) with yields unchanged. Dates explain about $3,390, curve assumption about $780. The sheet also stores a third figure ($295,924, headroom $4,076, 13.4bp) in results.json, and its code comment says the gap is ~$200 (it is ~$1,470). Mixing bases moves the IBTR test's goalposts by ~14bp and makes TNA and IPS disagree.

title: IBTR 'enough for all ten payments' depends on coupon reinvestment; no reflection may say 'locked' or 'secured'
problem: On the WInS holdings each payment is part principal, part coupons that must be reinvested at unknown rates. The 16 Oct sheet finds a delivery shortfall of about $21k if yields fall 2 points and stay there, and the IPS's own chain (leftover, Laura's half, gift above floor) fails to cover a small part in about 6-7 of 100 paths. The IBTR note's 'enough to buy Treasuries for all ten payments' is true only at today's forward reinvestment rates. A TNA reflection calling the payments 'locked', 'secured' or 'certain' would conflict with the IPS the team is about to adopt. The five T-bond notes already admit reinvested coupons fund part of each payment, so the team's own record supports an honest framing.
